title: Hustlers and number men at the Vendome Hotel
summary: Crawford describes the numbers bankers who stayed at the hotels and the Core and Claw families of Buffalo, with a detour on food at the Howard.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: What like -- besides musicians, what kind of people -- what kind of people would be in the hotels?
No, I mean -- I don't mean racially. I mean like what -- what kind of occupations did they have, what kind of work were they doing?

Oh, you had guys, hustlers there and everything. Person like like Jones Brothers out of Chicago, big number men. Now, you can erase that. And [Ruby] Harris out of Pittsburgh. When they hit Buffalo -- that's the only place I knew them, and I wanted to know more of them because they were

money men. [Ruby] Harris hit Buffalo, prices skyrocketed. He'd foot the bill. He was a big number man also out of Pittsburgh. Jones brothers, Ed and Mack Jones out of Chicago, yeah, they were -- and Bill [Core,] he owned the Vendome Hotel. It was a nice little hotel. Kept it very clean. He had a sister in Washington, Washington, by the name of Jean [Core.] She had a restaurant there.
And a hotel, but greatest food I ever -- during those -- during that period was a woman right behind -- what theater was that, Alene, that we used to --
Oh, the Howard Theater in Washington?

Yeah. We used to go in a dinnertime. You see, in Memphis when I was coming up, I didn't know anything about dinner. Everything was supper. As I said, homemade biscuits biscuits in the morning for breakfast, and corn bread, water, hot water, corn bread in the afternoon. That's the only bread I knew.
And we didn't call like oven -- brick oven bread like Arnold's (inaudible), we called that light bread.
That was -- well, it's -- I had great experiences.
But now like -- well now, sort of like
-- so then you mean in the -- the -- a lot of the people the musicians came in contact with then in terms of hotels were hustler -- hustling people.

Yes, most of them in the Vendome. But Bill Claw owned the hotel, had another brother who was the biggest -- big number man in Buffalo -- by the name of Joe Claw, big lanky, and another brother by the name of George Claw. He lived in the Vendome. Joe Claw lived out in north Buffalo or somewhere up there. I never got too close to Joe, not that I didn't want to, just never happened. George Claw I knew well because he was just a commoner.
